about: Kolkata-based company that sells imitation (fashion) jewellery made through contract manufacturers and wholesales it to distributors, dealers and retailers, mainly under the City Girl and Manikya brands. It also trades branded cosmetics and earns small rental and commission income. Revenue was Rs 30.36 crore in FY26, about 95% from B2B sales and about 66% from West Bengal.
sector: Imitation Jewellery and Cosmetics Trading (Gems, Jewellery and Watches)

objects.purpose: New plating facility at Baruipur, Kolkata
New B2B showroom at Ezra Street, Kolkata
Interiors and furnishing of B2C showrooms in Kolkata
Inventory for the proposed new showroom and stores

promoters.background: Mohammed Usman started in fashion jewellery retail in 2003 and took over the company in 2015 to enter contract manufacturing. Promoters are family members who run the business.

concentration.note: Top 5 customers 11.11% and top 10 customers 15.15% of FY26 sales (top 10 was 21.61% in FY24). West Bengal gave 65.77% of FY26 revenue; B2B was 95.16%.

litigation_note: 5 tax proceedings against the company involving about Rs 34.19 lakh in total; no criminal, regulatory or civil cases against the company, promoters or directors. An outstanding TDS demand of Rs 800 is also disclosed.
strengths: Revenue grew 70.8% in FY26 to Rs 30.36 crore and PAT rose to Rs 6.29 crore from Rs 2.00 crore.
Asset-light model: products are made by contract manufacturers, keeping fixed assets and debt low (debt/equity 0.17 at June 2026).
Broad customer base of about 800 retailers, 556 dealers and 12 distributors; top 10 customers are only 15.15% of sales.
Two brands, City Girl (gold-plated wedding and daily wear) and Manikya (CZ/AD), sold across 120 shop-in-shop counters.
ROCE of 57.74% and RoNW of 38.90% in FY26 on a small capital base.
Sells through a B2B showroom, shop-in-shop counters and e-commerce sites; owns a G+4 building in Rash Behari Avenue for B2C retail.
Cosmetics trading alongside jewellery gives retail customers one-stop supply and supports repeat wholesale orders.

risks.title: Weak cash flow and heavy working capital need
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative in FY24 (Rs -0.26 crore) and FY26 (Rs -0.68 crore) despite rising profits; inventory rose to Rs 7.83 crore and receivables to Rs 3.42 crore in FY26. Working capital cycle was 64 days in FY26 and 179 days for the June 2026 stub.

risks.title: Profit quality and valuation
risks.detail: FY26 other income of Rs 1.18 crore is almost entirely a one-time gain on a sale, so PBT without it is lower. IPO cap price of Rs 82 is 14.67x FY26 EPS of Rs 5.59, after EPS was only Rs 1.78 in FY25.

risks.title: Rising receivables and slowing inventory turnover
risks.detail: Debtor days went from 16 (FY24) to 30 (FY26) and 55 in the stub; inventory days rose from 38 to 117. Delayed collections or unsold stock could hurt cash and profits.

risks.title: Related party dealings
risks.detail: Related party transactions were Rs 3.28 crore (10.79% of revenue) in FY26 and 21.43% of revenue in the June 2026 stub; they were 66.40% of revenue in FY24.

risks.title: Dependence on contract manufacturers, no order book
risks.detail: Products are made by third-party contract manufacturers and produced on forecast demand, not confirmed orders. Company has limited own manufacturing experience and no registered IP on its designs.

risks.title: Regional and channel concentration
risks.detail: West Bengal contributed 65.77% of FY26 revenue and B2B 95.16%; a local slowdown or loss of wholesale buyers in Kolkata would hit revenue.

risks.title: Use of proceeds not appraised; property not finalised
risks.detail: Listed objects total about Rs 27.5 crore plus general purposes; these are management estimates not appraised by any bank. The new showroom property is only under an MOU with no definitive sale agreement yet.

risks.title: Promoter control, new listing and compliance gaps
risks.detail: Promoters hold 99.61% now and 72.22% after the issue; shares have no trading history on NSE Emerge. Company was not registered under ESIC in FY24 and FY25 and has 5 tax cases (Rs 34.19 lakh).

notes: Standalone restated financials (no subsidiaries mentioned), converted from Rs lakh. Stub period to 30-Jun-2026 ignored in arrays: revenue Rs 7.49 crore, PAT Rs 1.83 crore, net worth Rs 17.99 crore, borrowings Rs 3.06 crore, total debt/equity 0.17, NAV Rs 15.99. RHP prints a price band of Rs 77-82 but offer amounts in rupees are blank, so fresh_issue_cr and total_issue_cr are null (42,67,200 shares x Rs 82 would be about Rs 34.99 crore at cap). The restated balance sheet tables were not in the extracted text, so total_assets and current_ratio are null; reserves = net worth minus share capital (share capital Rs 0.66 crore FY24-25, Rs 11.25 crore FY26 after bonus). EBITDA is operating EBITDA excluding other income (matches reported margins); reported EBITDA including other income was Rs 1.29, 3.03, 8.52 crore. ROCE FY24 shown as 13.32% in one table and 13.42% in another. debt_equity computed as borrowings / net worth (only stub 0.17 reported). nav_per_share is FY26 (FY25 NAV Rs 148.82 was before share-capital increase). pe_pre_ipo is at cap price on FY26 EPS. reservation_pct is of net offer to public (40,52,800 shares); 2,14,400 shares reserved for the market maker; no anchor portion. Peer table has one peer (Banaras Beads) with revenue not given.
